en: The Parājikā spoken by the illustrious Lokeśvara.
Oṃ, homage to the Lord of the World!
In the beautiful and glorious land of Uttarakuru, she questioned the Lord of the World.
The goddess Tārā is of great compassion for the sake of the welfare of human beings.
And also the examination of the auspicious and inauspicious nature of the signs of portents.
O Lord, ocean of compassion, please teach [us] according to the proper method and with promptitude.
Lokeśvara said:
Listen, Tārā, I shall explain the procedure for pacifying portents.
For in the future time, people will indeed be of sinful conduct.
Calamity arises from sin; it perishes when one is dear to the Rite.
Therefore, for the sake of the welfare of the world, I have not spoken falsely.
Likewise, [one should offer] upon the garments of deities such as Dhvaja, or upon one's own garments.
A complete and thick image suddenly arises; hear about that.
O Lord, [the obstacle] perishes either in one year or in six months.
For that, there is the rite of the Five Protections and the great bali offering for pacification.
The gift of land, the gift of gold, the practice of begging for alms, and the eating of food.
By performing this, its pacification occurs; such is the certainty. ||1||
Beasts such as tigers and the like may suddenly appear in a region, a village, or even within a house.
Therefore, when they enter [that state], there arises the great terror of their master's death.
Its pacification is achieved through the recitation of *homas*, by the offering of great *bali* oblations,
by the gift of land and gold, and by feeding mendicants and preceptors.
On the day [of the eclipse], there is the falling of the serpent-king as well as Indra’s bow (the rainbow).
If, through a stroke of lightning, there should be destruction in this family here;
During the rites of pacification, fire-offerings, and worship, one should perform the worship of one's chosen deity according to the prescribed rules.
And one should cause the worship of the planets, as well as their recitation and the offering of oblations, to be performed.
The gift of land, gold, and houses, as well as providing food for one's teachers and others.
Peace is brought about by this which has been spoken by the Lord of the World.

O Lord, there will be the smell of water in wells, drains, and the like; likewise, there may be death, or else the destruction of friends and kinsmen, as well as the loss of various tastes, colors, and insects.
For the rite of pacification (śānti), there is this bell-metal vessel for the water-sacrifice (jalayajña) and the copper vessel for milk with molasses.

The Lord declares that by giving a bell-metal vessel with ghee, accompanied by a cloth, along with a golden-embryo jar filled with water, and by performing worship at wells and other such sites, peace is indeed attained. ||4||
In whichever house there suddenly arises the smell of a cremation ground even without fire or smoke, or various fragments of animal carcasses, and there is great terror as well as the fear of fire;
And there is death;
or within a month or five years, disputes, suffering, and quarrels occur.
One should effect its pacification within ten days by the offering of a golden image;
through the worship of one's own tutelary deity and the feeding of monks, pacification occurs constantly by this means. ||5||
Due to a fight between cats, there will be conflict even within the home with kinsmen, friends, and others;
for eight months, one shall experience the suffering of grief for women, distress, and quarrels.
They exist eternally.
One should perform a bath at a pure, excellent sacred site (tīrtha) at dawn, as well as the worship of the water-pot (kalaśa) and the ritual of fire-oblation (homa); furthermore,
one should give a silver image of a cat and provide food to a Brahmin.
At that very moment, there is peace. ||6||
There will be the entry of a snake into the house, or even a fall, and the death of the master; by this [dream], death occurs within five months or three.
Alternatively, there is the destruction of the husband, friends, and kinsmen, as well as the loss of wealth.
Peace must be established for him; one should not let it exceed seven days.
Having bathed at a sacred ford (tīrtha) at dawn and so forth, one should construct mandalas according to the prescribed rite.

One should perform oblations with the three sweets (*trimadhu*), the three myrobalans (*triphalā*), and iron (*loha*), using fuel-sticks of *śirīṣa* wood; one should offer seven thousand oblations of rice and other grains, as well as the seeds of the seven vegetables, with the mantra for the eradication of obstacles.
Along with fish, meat, and blood, as well as milk and curd.
One should cause the remnants of the offering to be given according to the prescribed rite when there is apprehension of snakes.

Taking the corpse of the deceased and offering an oblation upon that ground, one should strike it with mustard seeds alone; thus one should perform the ritual bath for the dead to release them from death.
One should cause the recitation of the *Pañcarakṣā* and other such texts, as well as the offering of moon-discs and other items.
Having given gold as a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) and provided food for the monks and the preceptor, those filled with compassion declare that by this means, that [evil] is pacified. ||7||
For when death occurs unexpectedly in the home, its fruit is even greater;
therefore, a wise person should have that [rite] performed according to the prescribed method preceded by pacification (śānti). ||8||
If, suddenly, a garland of house-mice (*gṛhacchucchulikā*) appears in the home,
it leads to grief; however, through propitiation, there is no destruction, and the loss caused by separation from one's wife is averted.
For its pacification, one should cause a vessel of jaggery to be offered along with gold.
Having offered the bali-oblation to Vighnāntaka, one should worship Gaṇeśa. ||8||
If a dog urinates on someone's limb, that person faces great danger,
loss of wealth, a severe illness, and the destruction of their family.
Its pacification occurs within two years by means of rice sprouts and boiled rice.
Having assumed the form of a dog and being provided with thirty-two offerings, one should worship it with the five-fold service (*pañcopacāra*) and cast it into clarified butter (*ghṛta*).

One should pacify [the affliction] immediately by means of this: a gift of silver or gold, or an image accompanied by molasses, along with a sacrificial fee of gold and the feeding [of Brahmins]. ||10||
If a dog with a bit is seen on its haunches, the result is as previously described.

And peace should be performed as previously described, as ordained by the Lord of the World. (11) [71] If a vessel filled with food, rice, and so forth, water, milk, ghee, or wine, is broken, the death of its owner will occur within a year or a month.
For its pacification, one should give gold, the gift of a cow, and food for monks;
and one should cause a golden-embroidered cloth and a full pitcher to be given.
If the death of a living being, or its body, is seen anywhere— in a monastery, in a village, on the ground, or even in a temple— the result [of that omen] is determined by that.
It will come to pass either in one year or within four months.
The great suffering of the master’s death, the great disease, and the great fear.
For his pacification, one should bathe at dawn in sacred bathing places and offer sesame seeds and gold.
One should cause to be given a copper vessel together with black gram and gold.
By this, peace is brought about, as spoken by the Lord of the World. ||13||
In a chariot, a temple, a shrine, a palace, or a pavilion;
It is especially the crest-jewel of the parasol, banner, flag, and so forth.
The water-pot, the arrow, the thunderbolt, and likewise the divine ornament.
Sudden falling, breaking, and burning by fire;
Or rather, his fear will consist precisely in various forms of perversion.
There shall be the fear of pestilence, the fear of fire, and the disintegration of the kingdom.
Various disputes and quarrels, famine, and the loss of wealth.
These [rites] are performed in the fifth month and also in the seventh year.
When they exist, one should reach the certainty that "peace shall not be made."
I shall proclaim their pacification for the sake of the pacification of Mahāmāyā and the others.
One should perform a fire sacrifice of one thousand oblations, recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times,
practice the fivefold protection known as the *Pañcarakṣā*, and likewise give gifts of cows and land.
Gold, the five kinds of food, and clothing—these are for the Brahmins and those who are monks.
Peace comes through this which has been spoken by the Lord of the World. ||14||
Whenever various wonders should suddenly occur in a temple,
then it is certain that the death of its presiding deity will occur within a year;
one should perform the propitiation of that very deity through worship according to the prescribed rites.
One should cause the gift of gold, the worship of Kaumārī, and the offering of a bali-oblation to be performed. ||15||
Various flowers and fruits arise that do not grow out of season.
Then that fear of the time passes away in an instant, even if it is raining.
One should perform the worship of the nine planets, the giving of gifts, and likewise the offering of bali to the local deities; by this, their pacification occurs—this is a firm certainty. (16)
The fruits of the *kuṣmāṇḍa*, *bījapūra*, and other such trees are clearly manifest.
And sprouts are seen within its interior; there is no doubt about this.
The lineage will perish and a wicked lineage will arise; of this there is no doubt.
There will be separation from one's own kin, as well as from friends and relatives.
Having fully worshipped the ritual jar (kalaśa) and other items, one should cause the great offering (mahābali) to be presented.
And one should give fruits and the like, as well as gifts of golden images, to a monk.
And one should also provide food according to one's ability; by this, peace is certain.
When a sprout is seen to have emerged from ripe grain and the like;
Then the former fruit shall arise, and his peace shall be as it was before. ||18||
If a fish is caught in a temple or even in one's own house,
its owner will die within a year, and his family shall also perish.
She should perform a peace-offering (śānti-homa) with gold, grain, sesame seeds, and so forth.
The giving of food to the Saṅghas is the certain means by which peace is attained. ||19||
Suddenly, by means of gold, silver, and various kinds of precious gems.
Then his wife and other dependents perish along with him.
For its pacification, one should cause various jewels, such as gold and so forth, to be given.
Likewise, one should worship the deity according to the ritual procedure for the worship of the Nāgas. ||20||
Even by the shaking of palaces or the shifting of the earth,
deities, shrines, chariots, gateways, and mountains may suddenly [fall],
as may the inner chambers of palaces and houses, especially due to the loss of their crest-jewels. (73)
He will suffer a broken limb, a fall, and even great terror.
There will be the death of the master, separation, and quarrels with kinsmen;
therefore, one should perform a peace-offering (śānti-homa) according to the rules, as well as the offering of oblations (bali-dāna).
One should also bestow gifts of cattle, land, and gold, and cause the *Pañcarakṣā* to be recited.
And when it is consumed by monks and preceptors, peace will certainly prevail; this is certain. ||21||
Of temples, deities, trees, and especially of one's own body.
By whomsoever no shadow is seen, by him death shall come to pass.
Then, either within six months or a year, his wife perishes.
For its pacification,
one should offer a golden image along with unbroken grains in a copper vessel.
Having established the mandala and performed the consecration and the worship of the ritual jars (kalaśa), [he should proceed].
One should give that gift and food with devotion to the Vajrācārya.
By this, peace has been spoken by the eternal Lord of the World. ||22||
Or like flowers produced from rotten seeds in a field characterized by its specific appearance and soil.
Through its adverse influence, his wife will become a destroyer;
within six months, there will be loss of wealth and quarrels.
The offering of oblations at the sacred sites and the sprinkling of water from the ritual pitcher.
The sin of giving land and the sin of taking silver are both pacified by the gift of food.
Why would the discovery of a dead corpse in the house bring about fear of impurity?
He faces the fear of his master's death for one year; of this there is no doubt.
Śānti, the monthly oblation sacrifice (māsāhuti-yajña), and likewise the offering of funeral cakes (piṇḍadāna).
The worship of Kṣatrapāla consists of a golden image in the form of a ball.
The offering of bali-oblations to the pretas and the feeding of the monks and preceptors.
By this eternal peace, there is indeed [peace] for him regarding the corpse of the dead.
The sudden collapse and breaking of palaces and gateways;
and the offering of libations with the remnants of food, radiant with a hundredfold light.
Taking earth from a broken place or from a quadrangular spot, one should offer that bali-oblation and cast it into the forest; as for the gift, it consists of gold, molasses, and clarified butter.
One should also perform the worship of Kaumārī and the Gaṇacakra.
By this, one who possesses compassion comes to know peace. ||24||
He who perceives a flaw in a star, or in the moon or the sun.
There will be great pestilence, famine, and fear in this place.
Its pacification is the recitation of the Mahāpañcarakṣā and the great bali offering.
The great sacrifice and the great gift of cows, gold, sesame seeds, and so forth.
An excellent gift such as a lunar disc, a solar disc, copper, pearls, and so forth, as well as food to be eaten immediately, should be given; by this, peace is certain. (25)
When the sudden liberation of the sun is attained through its manifestation.
Then death is attained either from a swing, a horse, or a vehicle, or from falling.
The wise man should perform its pacification over the course of a year, as previously described.
The consecrated water from the jar was suddenly spilled elsewhere, away from the ritual bath.
If the drying up or the nectar within it is broken, the master perishes.
There will be danger from fire for a year and a month, as well as various other dangers.
He fears the destruction of his undertakings; peace is attained through the worship of the water-pot.
The gift of land, the gift of gold, and likewise the feeding of virgins, as well as offerings to the Saṅghas according to one's ability—it is certain that through this there is peace. (27)
If, at the time of the fire-oblation, the extinction of the fire occurs suddenly,
it destroys the sacrificer and his family within seven months or seven years.
For its pacification, one should again perform a fire oblation (homa) as well as the worship of the planets;
through this knowledge of the lunar orb and so forth, pacification is certain.
If [the bird] cries during the worship of the gods and offerings, during the satiation of buffaloes, goats, and other animals,
or during the voiding of excrement, there will be a loss of blood and a lack of strength.
(75) Because of that, the death of the master shall occur in five months or one year.
Furthermore, for its pacification, one should worship the deity and perform a libation.
Having made gifts of cattle, land, and gold, one should provide a feast; and from the sale of elephants, horses, goats, sheep, and other vehicles, [one should likewise perform such acts].
Indeed, his wife perishes along with him as he goes to death;
for him, peace is fashioned in the form of an image of a vehicle.
One should offer that gift to the Vajrācārya and perform a *gaṇacakra* feast,
whether death from snakebite has suddenly occurred at home or due to some other cause.
If the master of the house meets death within seven days or a month,
one should perform a pacification rite by offering oblations into the mandala fire according to the prescribed ritual.
Likewise, there should be three copies each of the Pañcarakṣā, the Trivartapa, and the Āṅgirasa;
and a copper vessel twenty-five *ala* in size, filled with sesame seeds.
Having obtained a golden vessel covered with a white cloth,
salt and food should be offered to the Vajrācārya.
Through this certainty, there is a deliverance that brings peace;
by sowing seed in a field and so forth, that which was not born previously comes into being.
The death of its owner occurs within half a month or half a fortnight;
one should perform oblations in a sacrifice at that place and worship Kṣetrapāla.
A bell-metal vessel filled with ghee, an image joined with the moon,
the offering of gold as a circumambulatory gift, and food should be given to the most excellent assembly of noble ones.
By this truth, peace has been proclaimed by the best of sages for the occurrence of sudden earthquakes and the shaking of houses, fields, and other such places.
Therefore, there will be various fears, disease, and loss of wealth;
the pacification of that [misfortune] occurs through the drawing of the golden image of the House (Gṛha) accompanied by sesame seeds.

If a crow touches a specific limb during an act of charity to the deities of the quarters and so forth, during worship, or during a feast for the Saṅgha, it portends a sudden death; I shall now describe the results and the swift demise of the master. (76)
In the shoulder, there is loss of wealth and grief; in the throat, even quarrels arise.
If touched by a crow, one suffers stiffness in the hips, affliction of the feet by wind and other humors, and burning distress with grief in the stomach; such is the fruit of that touch.
One should perform the pacification rite for that [obstacle] by means of a sacrifice, bathing at a sacred ford with one's monastic robes,
worship of the nāgas, an offering (bali), and likewise an offering of water, unbroken rice grains, and a vessel of protection.
One should cause silver to be given as the moon and gold to be fashioned into the form of the sun for the Vajrācārya; thus, through the offering of golden dakṣiṇā, one becomes pure.
If lotus stalks are seen, yet devoid of pericarps,
she certainly meets with death and will surely experience grief.
To pacify that [evil], one should perform either a water-sacrifice or even a fire-sacrifice;
having gathered [the materials], one should again offer oblations a thousand times with the Tārā-mantra.
A vessel made of bell-metal filled with ghee, or one made of silver adorned with a moon,
should be given along with a white cloth and a meal of milk.
If smoke should arise unexpectedly from a house that is devoid of fire,
there will be the loss of his sons and the withering away of his fortune.
Its pacification consists of a great fire sacrifice (mahāhoma) and the worship of its presiding deity;
one should burn great incense and perform the offering of oblations (balidāna).
Suddenly, in the house, humans, elephants, horses, and cattle shall tear one apart;
through creatures such as those encountered during bathing and other activities, one encounters death by means of those who have already met their end.
Having gone to the confluence at that sacred ford (tīrtha) and bathed according to the prescribed rite,
one should perform the worship of the water-pot (kalaśa), the fire-oblation (homa), and give gifts along with a great sacrificial offering (mahābali).
By this, indeed, peace has been declared by the Lord of the World.
When [the sword] falls during worship while it is placed upon a stand, then there will be the death of its owner within four months; of this there is no doubt.
Since there may be grief caused by a woman, I shall indeed declare the means for its pacification:
the great recitation of the *Pañcarakṣā* and likewise the worship of Durgā. (77)
One should have the gift of a sword performed along with meat and gold.
The worship of one's own tutelary deity, as well as the feeding of mendicants and preceptors.
If a house has been built as a dwelling for crows in either a temple or a private home,
and they suddenly begin to converse there at twilight, that is its fruit.
There is fear of an enemy army in the east, and likewise fear of fire in the southeast;
in the southwest, there is the danger of the death of one's master and the threat of enemies;
in the west, there will be the destruction of the family; and in the northwest, the loss of sons.
In the north there will be loss of wealth; in the northeast, there will be extreme and great fear.
In the middle [of the practice], there may arise fear of kings and fear of untimely death;
I shall proclaim their pacification exactly as it was taught by the Tathāgata.
Having placed a copper vessel weighing three palas filled with the three sweets (trimadhu), along with a golden image of the deity, one should perform the worship of the pitcher (kalaśa).
One should perform the fire sacrifice (homa), the offering of oblations and food (balinaivedya), and the giving of garments and other items at the house;
one should then contemplate the withdrawal of the sword within the location of the Kākalāpa house.
Having sprinkled it with the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) as well as with water from ritual jars,
one should fumigate it there with mustard seeds and burn a crow's nest.
Having offered that ash as an oblation, one should cast it away in a forest area;
by this means, its pacification occurs—so it has been declared by the lords of sages.
If flowers produced on one tree grow upon another,
it portends the destruction of sons and daughters, as well as the loss of wealth within three months.
For its pacification, one should perform the recitation of the Mahāpañcarakṣā and a great bali offering; one should also cause a moon disc, a bronze vessel, curd, and milk to be presented.
Furthermore, by entering another house, one sees iron, snakes, and horses;
and from that, the downfall of one's wife and children is foretold.
